restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each pads to m || 0x86 (LSB-first bits 0,1,1,0,0,0,0,1 at state bits 1080..1087) in a single 136-byte rate block, capacity zero.
Uses the complete fixed-zero-state SHA3-256 sponge with prefix Keccak-f[1600] rounds 0 through 4 on every permutation call.

Self-contained algorithm in proof.md: embedded trail masks beta2, beta3, beta4 and connector target alpha2 (Section 3); exact two-round connector constraint system over message difference d and message values m (Section 4.3); per-instance message difference d_i is a connector output.

Finite caps: at most R = 2^13 connector successes, A = 2^4 attempts per success at a fixed per-attempt budget of 2^46.8 units, and at most E = 2^33 enumerated messages per affine space; failure is returned when caps are exhausted.
Charged: trail-search precomputation (2^60 envelope), all connector attempts including failures, brute-force hashing, scanning and final verification.

Analytical construction; a byte-aligned round-0 connector instance was produced and verified locally, but no complete two-round p = 8 connector instance, no full-scale execution, and no certificate are supplied.
The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement; the bound 64 under collision-frontier-v5 rests on declared heuristics h1-h4.

heuristics.statement: With the 0x86 byte-string tail (p = 8), a two-round connector for alpha2 succeeds within A = 2^4 attempts of 2^46.8 units each and returns an affine message space of dimension DF >= 25.
heuristics.scope: Prefix rounds 0-1 of Keccak-f[1600], rate 1088 / capacity 512, 135-byte messages; constraint system of proof Section 4.3.
heuristics.extrapolation: Published p = 4 connector: DF = 37 for 428.8 core-hours (about 2^46.2 units at 2^36 word-ops per core-second). Measured locally at p = 8: the round-0 layer for the published alpha1 is satisfiable (instance in proof Appendix A). Four extra fixed bits remove at most four degrees of freedom linearly.
heuristics.limitations: Measured pad sensitivity: with the witness's round-0 difference pattern fixed, the two-round system is satisfiable under tail 0xEE but not under 0x86; 25 other fixed patterns and a 240-280 s unpinned solve produced no p = 8 two-round instance. If p = 8 success needs more than about 2^4.6 times the published per-success connector work, the bound fails.

heuristics.statement: Each pair (m, m XOR d_i) in a connector space satisfies the zero digest-difference condition after rounds 2-4 with probability at least 2^-36.70.
heuristics.scope: Prefix rounds 2, 3, 4 of the exact profile; per-pair event over connector-produced pairs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Embedded beta2 -> alpha3 and beta3 -> alpha4 weights were recomputed exactly (24 and 19); the 2^-36.70 aggregate over compatible final-round trails is the published figure; the verified published witness follows beta2 and beta3 bit-for-bit.
heuristics.limitations: Published differential estimate, not a proof for the connector's output distribution.

heuristics.statement: Collision events across the R connector spaces count as approximately independent, so at least 2^37 tested pairs give expected collisions at least 1.23 and success above 0.70 under a Poisson approximation.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard counting convention for differential attacks; each space is built from fresh coins and a freshly drawn alpha1.
heuristics.limitations: Not proven. The declared 0.5 tolerates an effective-mean loss of only about 0.8 bit; no larger correlation tolerance is claimed.

heuristics.statement: The conversion of 2^36 word operations per core-second and the 2^60-unit envelope for trail-core search are upper-bound conventions for the respective work.
heuristics.scope: Connector budget and trail-search charge in proof Section 6.
heuristics.extrapolation: Published timing data; trail-search cost is not separately reported, so a large flat envelope is charged.
heuristics.limitations: Stated envelopes rather than instruction traces.
